name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.21.0 — `/spec:release`'s ~10-step prose checklist becomes a script, the same move `review-legs.js` made for review: `spec/scripts/release-legs.js` (`spec-paths release-legs`) owns every deterministic release leg through one `stage` subcommand — `substrate` (wraps `manifest-check.sh`), `deploy`, `ready` (a plain retried curl against the deployed `stagingUrl`+`healthPath`; `runtime.readyCheck`'s local-boot contract is the wrong host for a deployed URL, so release.md's old "readyCheck pattern applied to stagingUrl" phrasing — unimplementable as written — is retired, not reused), `migrations` (only when declared runnable), `e2e` (a widened typed-unavailability grammar so `passed`/`failed` admit the same `{"unavailable":…}` shape `skipped` already had — no assumed count without a declared format), and `ci` (the review-legs mapping plus the poll loop release.md used to prescribe in prose, now exactly one row appended per run, never per poll iteration) — plus `append` for the two session-observed legs (`journeys`, `production`) and `record` as the single `verdict.js --profile release --ledger` invocation point on every path alike, STOP and normal close, deriving `--require migrations` itself instead of three separate prose restatements. `release.md` shrinks to judgment steps only — grounding interview, manifest maintenance, journey walks, promote confirm, tag, report — citing the script's own header comment for every row grammar and the poll cadence rather than restating them, the fragile spot that had drifted. The feedback-brief flush retires everywhere it lived (`release.md` Phase 4, `doctor.md` check 12's offer clause, `spec/templates/feedback-brief.md` itself, and the `spec-paths feedback-template` key): its `/intake` consumer died in v7, core § Incident Policy bans intake queues, and § Feedback Loop's carrier list never named briefs — host→plugin signal rides run ledgers and `[plugin]`-tagged Gotchas only. (7.20.0 was the plan-time version target; a concurrent session had already taken it by build time, so this bump lands on the next free minor per the recorded semver-race gotcha.) 7.20.0 — `init.md` (604 lines, the last big English program standing after v7) is rewritten around one new script, `spec/scripts/init-gen.js` (`spec-paths init-gen`): `probe` reports read-only findings (`frontendDesign`, `testCommand`, `atRisk`) and always exits 0 on adverse findings — findings are data, never a probe failure; `generate` reads a session-authored profile JSON and becomes the sole writer of every grounding-layer deliverable (config, pipeline rules file, convention rules, agents, both skills, settings permissions merge, patterns script, manifest), enforcing manifest-check.sh-then-stamp ordering in code — a red manifest-check now structurally cannot leave a stamped config, closing a rule that was previously prose an interrupted session could violate. A spike falsified the locked `.claude/worktrees` idempotency check (`git check-ignore -q .claude/worktrees` exits 1 on a fresh host when the directory does not yet exist, even with the ignore entry present); the script probes a child path instead, and a test pins the corrected form. An existing target file that differs from what the profile would produce now refuses generation at exit 3 (nothing written) unless `--refresh` is passed, with `.claude/settings.json` always merge-preserving in both modes — re-running init can no longer silently clobber hand-edits; an existing settings file that does not parse as JSON is refused in pre-flight at exit 2 with nothing written (found at review 2026-08-23: the merge previously swallowed the parse error and rebuilt the file, destroying the host's permission allow AND deny entries at exit 0 with no warning). Three probes brief 11 named land: `frontend-design` install detection via `claude plugin list --json` (ADR-0001 — the script only detects, the interview only offers, the user only consents, with a typed `unavailable` fallback to asking directly), the `testCommand` no-match probe (the class behind the 2026-08-20 at-risk escape — a runner exiting 0 on a nonexistent path now surfaces in the interview and, once accepted, lands a permanently re-verifiable negated-`exec` manifest row), and `scope-reconcile.js`'s additive `--probe-at-risk` mode (its existing `--json`/`--dirs` modes byte-identical, pinned) disclosing when the at-risk review leg will likely never fire on a host. `tests/run-ledger.test.js`'s prose pin over init.md retargets to a behavioral test now that the union-driver instruction lives in code, not prose. 7.19.0 — a review that burns its fix loop to the cap (2 iterations) and is then abandoned no longer writes zero ledger rows: the cap refusal now appends an **escalate row** at the moment of the refusal, an honestly-derived non-CLEAN verdict carrying `escalated: true`, minted by `verdict.js` behind a new `--escalated` flag with `--fixDispatched 0` (the dispatched fix never landed; refused with `--fixDispatched > 0` or `--profile release`, and refused rather than printed when the derivation reaches CLEAN under evidence drift — a self-contradictory CLEAN+escalated row is the worst possible output the one file that must never wrongly say CLEAN could carry). `spec-review-driver.js`'s `writeEscalateRow()` runs the pass from `handleFixApplied()`'s cap branch before dying, reusing spec 04's stopped-ledger durability verbatim in a worktree (`<mainRoot>/.claude/spec-runs.stopped.jsonl`, drained into the tracked ledger at close positioned before the close row) and self-healing a missing append on a bare re-invocation via the sidecar's `escalateRunId` mark. The ESCALATE step text now names both exits — fresh dispositions (`--fix-dispatched 0` covering the pool) closing normally through the waive/reject route, or deleting the `<spec>.review/` sidecar to abandon and restart cold — plus the absolute path the row landed in; a new driver-entry detector warns (stderr-only, never blocking) when a sidecar-recorded durable path no longer has a readable row for the spec+runId. `spec/commands/review.md`'s ledger-append sentence now names ESCALATE alongside STOPPED and CLOSE, and its ESCALATE re-entrancy prose names the row and both exits. No new verdict word: the escalation fact rides as a typed row field, never a second place that derives or asserts CLEAN.
